function: Prediction of the departing LEO satellite's downlink CSI during handover from historical channel gains with a 2D-CNN (CNN-CSI), enabling joint precoding of two LEOs (p. 7).
system: LEO satellite phased array, 8 spot beams, N=4 transmit antennas, 45 single-antenna UEs, Rician channel; 2 GHz carrier, 100 MHz bandwidth; no RIS (p. 3, 12).
method: Supervised 2D-CNN regression (3 conv layers + FCNN) on historical channel gains, MSE loss, Adam; transfer learning freezes the first two layers, retrained at LEO 2 (p. 7-8).
data_channel: Custom simulation: 45 UEs in a Starlink footprint, Rician channel (κ=10 dB), Jakes model with AR(1) correlation ρ; 60x11 samples for train/validation/test; no 3GPP model (p. 4, 11).
test_conditions: Train/validation/test of 528/130/1 slots for each correlation coefficient (rho = 1, 0.9, 0); test input is the 659th slot of the same series; no unseen scenario (p. 11).
baselines: No learned baseline for CSI prediction; HO precoding with predicted CSI compared with Baselines 2-3 using pilot-based CSI estimation (non-learned), plus ZF and fixed-beam references (p. 12-14).
metrics: MSE of CSI prediction (Fig. 7); effective mean/min data rate, outage probability, content delivery delay, convergence iterations (p. 11-14).
complexity: Order of CNN-CSI training cost O(Emax*D*sum n_(l-1) s_l^2 n_l * 2U) (p. 8); K-means O(2MUImax+MKm) and SCA cost cubic in variables (p. 6); no runtime measured.
openness: none; only the public MovieLens 1M request dataset is used for content popularity, CSI data are simulated, no code or data link (p. 10).
q1_support: p. 11: "apply the Jakes model [49] to generate the channel matrix" - custom Rician/Jakes simulation with AR(1) correlation (p. 4, Table III); no 3GPP channel model, public ray-tracing dataset or measured data is used.
q2_support: p. 11: "datasets were generated with different correlation coefficient" - train and test sets are matched per rho and the test slot is the 659th of the same series (p. 11); transfer learning is only described (p. 8) and no result on an unseen scenario or after adaptation is reported.
q3_support: p. 12: "In this approach, both satellites estimate the CSI via pilot" - Baselines 1-3 are non-learned (ZF, optimal precoding, pilot-based CSI); no earlier or standard learned CSI predictor is compared with the CNN-CSI.
q4_support: p. 8: "1) Complexity of the Proposed Algorithm: The computational complexity to train" - the CNN-CSI, given as O(Emax D sum n s^2 n 2U) [41]; Algorithm 1 costs O(2MUImax + MKm) (p. 6).
q5_support: p. 10: "The content popularity is generated from the location-based" - public MovieLens 1M data serve only for content requests, not channels; the CSI data are simulated (p. 11); no code or data link is given.
notes: Included on the CNN-CSI only: the SCA precoding/bandwidth design and K-means++ spot-beam clustering (Algorithm 1, p. 5-6) are classical iterative algorithms, not counted as learned. Area 2 by function (channel prediction), not area 6; if the reviewer counts K-means as learned beam control, area 6 would apply. Satellite array with N=4 antennas, single-antenna UEs (MISO). Title and DOI checked on p. 1; Tables II-III read from the page image (p. 12).
